Drop (or flag) months that were not published yet

Source: R/publicacao.R
mds_drop_unpublished.Rd

The MI Social API answers 0, not "missing", for months whose data has not been published: the BPC series, for example, carries zeros for every municipality up to December of the current year. Treating those zeros as real would make the latest months look like a collapse of the programme.

mds_drop_unpublished(
  data,
  today = Sys.Date(),
  reference = c("selection", "brazil"),
  action = c("drop", "flag")
)

Arguments

data

A tibble returned by mds_data() or a theme shortcut.

today

Reference date for rule 1. Default Sys.Date().

reference

Where the last published month is read from: "selection" or "brazil". See Details.

action

"drop" (default) removes future and unpublished rows; "flag" keeps every row and adds the columns publication_status ("published", "future", "unpublished" or "missing"), publication_reason and publication_reference.

Value

data without the dropped rows, or with the classification columns. A message summarizes what was removed.

Details

This helper applies an explicit rule, per field:

  1. months after the current month are future;

  2. months after the last month with a non-zero value are unpublished;

  3. a field with no non-zero value at all is unpublished entirely.

The "last month with a non-zero value" comes from reference:

  • "selection" (default): the localities in data. Needs no request, but a small selection can legitimately end in zeros (a municipality without a CREAS unit, for example), and those zeros would be dropped.

  • "brazil": every municipality in the country, through mds_periods() (two facet requests per field when not cached). A month is unpublished only when no municipality in Brazil has a non-zero value, which keeps legitimate zeros of small selections.

A non-zero value in data is never classified as unpublished. If the national reference says a month with such a value is unpublished (a cached reference older than the data, for instance), the reference is requested again; if the contradiction remains, the month is kept and a warning is raised.

This is an inference from the published values, not an official publication date. A series can legitimately end in zeros, even nationally; use action = "flag" to inspect the classification before removing anything.

Rows with a missing value are never classified as zero: they are kept and flagged as "missing".

Examples

x <- tibble::tibble(
  locality_id = "261160", period = c("202506", "202507", "202508"),
  field = "bpc_ben_i", value = c(98000, 98500, 0)
)
mds_drop_unpublished(x, today = as.Date("2025-12-01"))
#> Dropped 1 row of trailing all-zero months:
#> • bpc_ben_i: 202508
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   locality_id period field     value
#>   <chr>       <chr>  <chr>     <dbl>
#> 1 261160      202506 bpc_ben_i 98000
#> 2 261160      202507 bpc_ben_i 98500
mds_drop_unpublished(x, today = as.Date("2025-12-01"), action = "flag")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   locality_id period field     value publication_status publication_reason      
#>   <chr>       <chr>  <chr>     <dbl> <chr>              <chr>                   
#> 1 261160      202506 bpc_ben_i 98000 published          NA                      
#> 2 261160      202507 bpc_ben_i 98500 published          NA                      
#> 3 261160      202508 bpc_ben_i     0 unpublished        after the last non-zero…
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: publication_reference <chr>
